question: P2
asked:
Which claims support, directly or through a chain of arguments, the thesis that vectorization needs a data source that returns columns? Do not include the thesis itself.

Answer format: in values only the nodes that are the answer, an element per node: key is the id, value the name.

answer.answer: Four claims support the thesis (claim_need_columnar) that vectorization needs a data source returning columns: two directly — claim_no_columnar_source (no storage in vanilla PostgreSQL 19 hands data column by column) and claim_skip_simulation (simulating page skipping made ClickBench queries many times faster); and two indirectly through claim_no_columnar_source — claim_citus_hydra_rows (Citus columnar and Hydra are columnar inside but hand out row slots) and claim_pax_aoco_patched (Greenplum's PAX and AOCO need a patched core).

values.value: On unmodified PostgreSQL 19 there is not a single storage that would hand the vectorized executor data column by column
A simulation of skipping unneeded pages made the same ClickBench queries many times faster
Citus columnar and Hydra are columnar inside, but through the tableAM API they hand out slots one row at a time
PAX and AOCO from Greenplum work only on the port's patched core, not on vanilla PostgreSQL

answer.answer: The thesis that vectorization needs a data source that returns columns is supported by claims stating that unmodified PostgreSQL 19 lacks such storage (claim_no_columnar_source), and that simulations of skipping unneeded pages significantly improved performance (claim_skip_simulation). The claim about the lack of storage is further supported by the fact that Citus columnar and Hydra still return data row by row through the tableAM API (claim_citus_hydra_rows), and that Greenplum's PAX and AOCO require a patched core rather than vanilla PostgreSQL (claim_pax_aoco_patched).

values.value: On unmodified PostgreSQL 19 there is not a single storage that would hand the vectorized executor data column by column
A simulation of skipping unneeded pages made the same ClickBench queries many times faster
Citus columnar and Hydra are columnar inside, but through the tableAM API they hand out slots one row at a time
PAX and AOCO from Greenplum work only on the port's patched core, not on vanilla PostgreSQL

)

values.value: On unmodified PostgreSQL 19 there is not a single storage that would hand the vectorized executor data column by column
A simulation of skipping unneeded pages made the same ClickBench queries many times faster

PAX and AOCO from Greenplum work only on the port's patched core, not on vanilla PostgreSQL

PAX and AOCO from Greenplum work only on the port's patched core, not on vanilla PostgreSQL
